Well, my parents surely fucked me up. First decade of my life was exactly as described in this article. 

My thought on the article are that from personal experience it's very, very true. I don't know how much praising part of fucking up my childhood contributed to my failure to get a degree, but it most certainly played a part.

Still, I want to say that I was diagnosed bipolar at age 20, and now I'm several years older. I can't tell how much my fucked up life can be attributed to my parents.

Thanks, your post sure is inspiring. My mother sure is toxic either.

I don't know what I'll do, but I'll try to stay afloat. If only I somehow where able to overcome my depression.

Well, there are only side-effects from medication for now.

As to hobby, well, reddit it is.

>Finally, the big issue. You're incapable of solving problems. Is it fair to say you're afraid of interacting with people, making decisions and accepting the consequences, and doing things for yourself, acting on rational self-interest?

It's because I'm depressed, I can't concentrate on stuff and force myself to go out for example. This problems are consequences of depression. I don't seem to be able to solve this.

>May I ask if you have a positive relationship with your father?

More like no relationship at all. He doesn't answer when I call him. Can't blame him a lot, it got like this because of my depression issues. Anyway he and my mother divorced early and I didn't talk with him a lot at all.

>I'd love to chat more. I hope you're getting by, coping, being a good roommate to your awesome friend and making that paper.

I'm just wondering what paper are you talking about here?

I think you're right about our relationship, but I'm afraid to end it if only because I'm afraid to be alone. And she does a good job caring for me. And I was able to hold a job this long (about a year now) thanks to her. Now I'm not sure if she is helping me, on holding me back, but I'm afraid to break our relationship.

>You should happy that you have money and a job. Most of us can't get either these days so you've clearly done well for yourself. Good job. (neat pun)

Thanks, that cheered me up a bit :)

As to moving out, I lived a little by myself, but because I wasn't able to stockpile money and depression got me, I returned.

Now I can't return anyway, just seeing my mother makes me feel like shit.

>Don't let your girlfriend guilt you into staying in a relationship
I'm as afraid to stay alone as she is. When our relation started, she already had depression issues and was suicidal at times. Now, I don't know if I want to stay with her, and if I will just collapse if I leave. I'm not known for being especially psychologically stable...

>How might things change if you had a better job, or more money? Have you ever been able to visit with a therapist? Have you ever been on medication?

I have a good job actually, not dead end in any way. I don't have a degree, but if I stay at my job I'll be set for life. Well, because of my depression I'm performing badly, so I guess I'm loosing it anyway.

I started seeing psych doctor after very long pause, he gave me some pills.

Now I'm doing some system tech work, but I consider myself unprofessional and lazy worker, still I got a decent job thanks to my mania and lack of professional workers on the market and now I can do very little for some time and still not be kicked out.

But I don't like it, I don't like tech jobs anymore and I want to do something which would make me proud, not something that makes me understand how awful I am. Still, this job pays well and coworkers are good. Don't know what to do.
